text: Khatia Dekanoidze - If we look at what is happening in Armenia, you will see that the role Georgia once had as a regional leader no longer exists—Georgia is losing this role because of Ivanishvili's crime and the "anti-Georgian Dream" (06.05.2026, 12:00)

"Today, Ivanishvili and the 'Anti-Georgian Dream' have deprived Georgia of its capacity for long-term peace, development, progress, and economic prosperity. They have robbed the Georgian people of the opportunity for well-being and wealth, and the opportunity for European integration. This is a historical crime," stated Khatia Dekanoidze, one of the leaders of the National Movement.

He congratulated the public on the "liberation of Adjara from the rule of Russia and a despot" 22 years ago on May 6, noting that this very day marked the start of a new chapter in Georgia's history, which signified the region's leadership.

“I congratulate you on one of the most distinguished dates in Georgia's recent history—the return of Adjara to Georgia. Exactly 22 years ago, on May 6, one of the most significant events in Georgia's recent history took place, when Adjara returned to the heart of Georgia, was liberated from Russian rule, liberated from the rule of a despot, and together with President Mikheil Saakashvili, his team, and many fervent patriots, a very important ascent began. And yes, Georgia started a new chapter, which meant regional leadership, development in technology and education, in the context of Eastern European expansion and the strategic partnership with the USA, which was truly our nation's historic mission. This was the day when we transitioned to a completely different level of state development, and our team truly managed to secure Georgia's role as a regional leader.

Today, Ivanishvili and the ‘Anti-Georgian Dream’ have caused Georgia to lose its role in long-term peace, development, progress, and economic prosperity. They have deprived the Georgian people of the opportunity for prosperity, enrichment, and European integration. This is a historical crime. If we look at what is happening in our neighbor Armenia—and I want to wish them great success—you will see that the role Georgia once had, to be a regional leader and to have many sustainable peace projects, no longer exists. The events unfolding in Armenia in recent days are not just about political support from the EU, the USA, or Canada for our neighbors; they are about investment projects that truly imply long-term peace.

We had many such projects; among them, Mikheil Saakashvili, who is now a political prisoner, was directly involved in the development and construction of the Batumi Technological University, and I myself am very proud to have participated in the construction of this university. This university was meant to become a truly significant hub for Georgia in education, technology, new communication systems, and the transition to a new stage of education. What has been happening in Armenia is not just political support, but economic support that ensures long-term peace. Everyone who was involved in the most important stages of Georgia's development is now watching how the country is losing this role due to Ivanishvili's crime and the ‘Anti-Georgian Dream.’ Georgia is losing 400 billion in investment, military-technological cooperation with France and the United States, energy security projects, and most importantly, the new corridor that the European Commission, the EU, the USA, and Canada are now discussing—massive investments that are among the most important fields for peace, sustainable development, and progress,” Dekanoidze stated.
